name: copper_placement_default
note: Settings for placing composed designs with the C placer (src/v2_src/placement.c via `copper-core place`). They are Copper's design choices, not fabricator capabilities; the router and DRC still check every clearance against the fab profile.

edge_mm.why: pad to board edge: twice the router's 0.5 mm copper-to-edge clearance (routing_profiles/copper_2layer_default.json), so a track can pass between a pad and the edge

gap_mm.why: courtyard to courtyard: room for one 0.25 mm track with 0.3 mm clearance is not guaranteed by this alone; the router re-checks every clearance

body_margin_mm.why: no part body within 2.5 mm of the board edge: the design compiler and the grounding gate require every part origin at least 2.5 mm inside the board, and an origin lies inside its part's body

step_mm.why: placement grid, the step tools/layout.py used with the same placer

area_weight_per_mm2.why: tools/layout.py WEIGHTS placement_area_mm2: a small pull toward a compact placement

decoupling_weight_per_mm.why: tools/layout.py WEIGHTS decoupling_mm: a decoupling capacitor is pulled toward its IC

keepout_edge_weight_per_mm.why: tools/layout.py WEIGHTS keepout_edge_mm: a part keep-out (the ESP32-S3 antenna zone) is pulled toward the board edge

fine_pitch_gap_mm.why: Step 3c, LAYOUT_RULES.md R5: a part whose own pads (different nets) are closer than this is fine-pitch; equal to the router's clearance_mm (routing_profiles/copper_2layer_default.json), the same test the router uses

fine_pitch_escape_mm.why: room for a fine-pitch part's escape stubs: an escape end cell needs half a track + clearance + the router's grid slack (0.125 + 0.3 + 0.1875 = 0.6125 mm) from every other-net pad, about 1.5 mm from the pad row to the next part's pad; a SOT-563 courtyard is only 0.15 mm beyond its pads and gap_mm adds 0.5 mm, so the body grows by 1.0 mm (about 0.7 mm is the least that works)

iterations.why: annealing moves per seed; seconds for boards of tens of parts

seeds.why: independent annealing runs; the lowest-cost legal one is kept, so the result is deterministic
